meta.requirement: Explore Wolvendom (30%+ exploration) to trigger this quest.

customTabs.label: TIP
customTabs.content:
You can click the '''Collapse''' button and the '''Best Route''' → '''Important Only''' button at the top to minimize it.
''Some quests will not have a Best Route choice, because the best choice is subjective or not yet found.''

You can also click the '''Endings''' button at the top to view all possible endings, and clicking an ending will show the options needed to reach that ending.

start.title: Frost on the Trail
start.text:
''You hear a bowstring ease off before you see the archer.''

Elle: ''from a low ridge, not aiming at you'' Hold. Feet still. They can hear more than they should today.

''Below the ridge, two Cryo Hilichurls crouch over torn wolfhook vines. A Cryo Samachurl chants behind them, frost gathering on the bark.''

Elle: ''quiet'' Pack got shoved out of its usual ground. Something colder is pushing them west. I can put arrows in the little ones. The big problem is further in.

Need_a_blade_for_this.text:
Elle: Clear the pack so they stop pushing toward Springvale. Then we follow whatever shoved them. Prints are wrong. Heavy. Icy shells, not stone.

Elle: Stay if you can fight. Leave if you like the idea of me yelling at trees alone. I will manage. Badly.

choices.label: I'll clear the pack with you

I_will_clear_the_pack_with_you.text: Elle: ''nocks an arrow'' Good. Pack first. Samachurl dies early if you can help it. Then we move before the woods get ideas.

dialogues.speaker: 📌 Objective
dialogues.text: Clear the cryo hilichurl pack near Elle in Wolvendom

continues.label: Do /rpg again and click on Fight the Cryo Pack. Defeat 2 [[Cryo Hilichurl]]s and 1 [[Cryo Samachurl]]

You_re_hunting_alone_.text:
Elle: Was. Then the trail got bigger than my quiver.

Elle: I am not dying pretty for Springvale coin. I am finishing the job.

Fight_the_Cryo_Pack.text:
''The last Cryo Hilichurl drops. Frost fades off the wolfhook vines.''

Elle: ''low whistle'' Clean enough.

Elle: Trail keeps going. Smell of ozone under the cold. Not normal for this ridge. Stay close. The next group already knows we are moving.

dialogues.speaker: 📌 Objective
dialogues.text: Follow Elle deeper into Wolvendom and break the next ambush

continues.label: Do /rpg again and click on Break the Ambush. Defeat 1 [[Cryo Hilichurl]], 1 [[Hilichurl Berserker]], and 1 [[Electro Slime]]

Break_the_Ambush.text:
''An Electro Slime's spark dies in the snowmelt. The berserker stops moving. The hilichurl does not get back up.''

Elle: ''kicks a spent arrow, then looks past you'' There. The prints stop playing coy.

Elle: Frostarm Lawachurl. Should be on Dragonspine, not chewing Wolvendom into new borders. Ready when you are. I will not waste arrows pretending I can solo that shell.

dialogues.speaker: 📌 Objective
dialogues.text: Hunt the Frostarm Lawachurl with Elle in Wolvendom

continues.label: Do /rpg again and click on Hunt the Frostarm Lawachurl. Defeat 1 [[Frostarm Lawachurl]] and 1 [[Cryo Samachurl]]

Hunt_the_Frostarm_Lawachurl.text:
''The Frostarm Lawachurl hits the dirt hard enough to shake pine needles loose. Its icy shell cracks, then goes quiet.''

Elle: ''exhales through her teeth'' That. That was the shove.

Pack_should_settle_now.text:
Elle: ''ties a scrap of frost-cracked shell into her satchel'' Proof for the desk hunters who never leave town.

Elle: You took the hits I could not. That is worth silver and a name I will remember when someone asks who walks Wolvendom without flinching.

____Frost_on_the_Trail__Trail_Closed.title: Trail Closed
____Frost_on_the_Trail__Trail_Closed.text:
Elle: ''nods once'' Pack pushed west. We pushed back. That is the whole poem.

Elle: If the shells show up again, I will send word. Prefer your company to another lonely ridge.

''She fades back toward the Springvale path, cloak patched, trail already half her attention again.''

What_will_Springvale_say_.text:
Elle: They will say thanks, count the meat, and ask why I came back with a story that sounds like a lie.

Elle: Let them. The trail does not care who believes it.
